title: Coming soon - the Find Our Fungi app!
text:
Fungi have often been the Cinderella of conservation: beautiful, hardworking but overlooked. Thankfully, there is a growing awareness that fungi need protection just as much as plants and animals do. We have the privilege to be running a major research programme supplying evidence-based conservation strategies for 12 of Britain’s threatened fungi. This is being funded by DEFRA through Natural England as part of the Species Recovery Programme, which focuses on moving conservation forward in the areas identified in the Threatened Species Recovery Actions.
However, we need your help! The very rarity of these fungi makes them hard to find; some have only been recorded 20 times in the last hundred years. If we are to get a good idea of the current population, we will need to recruit as many eyes on the ground (or the tree trunks) as possible. To that end, we are asking people to report sightings of these twelve species via our custom app. To help you get familiar with them, we have produced a handy fold-out leaflet with pictures and key facts about each one.

Coming soon - the Find Our Fungi app!

title: About us
text:
The Cardiff fungi group started out in 1986, when Lynne Boddy arrived at what was then University of Wales College, Cardiff. Over time, UWCC became Cardiff University, and the fungi research group moved around different campus locations until finally settling on the sixth floor of the Sir Martin Evans Building. The group has been composed of an ever-changing kaleidoscope of postdocs, technicians PhD students, master’s students and undergraduates. Many of those who joined the group in one role have stayed on to take up another; technicians and master’s students have become PhD students, and PhD students have become postdocs.
In 2023, a former PhD student, Sarah Christofides, gained a lectureship at the School of Biosciences and rejoined the group to co-lead it alongside Lynne. Lynne and Sarah have worked together for many years and provide complementary skills and experience which have allowed the group to go from strength to strength. As a group, we pride ourselves on being an exceptionally friendly and supportive team, where is member is valued as an individual and where helping each other is our modus operandi. Team lunch breaks, regular inclusive socials and a collective silly sense of humour all help foster a sense of team identity where everyone is welcome.

title: Cardiff Fungal Ecology Group
text:
Welcome to Fungal Ecology Cardiff, the official website for the internationally-renowned fungi group at Cardiff University. Led by Professor Lynne Boddy and Dr Sarah Christofides, we research many kinds of fungal interactions in the environment. We specialise in tree-associated fungi, particularly wood-decay basidiomycetes. In these pages you can find information on our team, research, and educational activities.
We are based in Cardiff School of Biosciences and affiliated to the Organisms and Environment research division.
Disclaimer: all content on this website represents the views of individual members of the fungi team, and not Cardiff University or the School of Biosciences.
